title: Session 1 — Participant 29 User + Claude Behavior Graphs
goal: Prepare the construction-management workbook for Power BI reporting and begin development of a reliable reporting data structure.
context:
I created a Google Sheets–based construction management system for a small contractor. The workbook is used to track projects, employee and contractor time, labor and material costs, project budgets, quotes, and invoices. The long-term goal is to connect the operational workbook to Power BI so that the business owner can review project performance without manually combining information from multiple worksheets.
During this session, I initially planned to progress from reviewing the workbook through development of a Power BI dashboard. In practice, reviewing the existing data structure, determining reporting requirements, preparing data for reporting, and working with Claude took more time than expected. Claude's responses were slower than anticipated, so I revised the workflow after the session to more accurately represent the work completed.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: I made progress identifying the reporting requirements and determining how the operational workbook needed to be structured for Power BI. However, I did not progress as far into Power BI development as originally planned. A significant amount of the session was spent reviewing the workbook, evaluating Claude's recommendations, refining the proposed data structure, and waiting for Claude to complete requests. The original goal was too broad for the available session time.

Step 1.step_action: I will review the existing construction-management workbook to identify the tabs, fields, formulas, and records that can support management reporting. I will ask Claude to analyze the available data structure, identify missing information, and recommend the most valuable KPIs and dashboard pages for a small construction business.

nodes.label: Pivoting to dashboard planning

nodes.label: Delivering the KPI recommendation list
nodes.detail: Lays out five focus areas for the dashboard -- budget health (utilization %, remaining budget, an at-risk-projects list), labor cost breakdown by project/contractor/work type, contractor activity via days-worked rather than hours, a project timeline view, and data-quality flags (open sessions, missing GPS/duties) -- plus a critical gotcha: the workbook pays a flat day rate, so a DAX measure must not multiply Hours x Pay Rate, and should instead count distinct (contractor, project, work-date) sessions per day rate, mirroring the existing Labor by Project logic.

rubrics: Recommendations reflect the information actually available in the workbook.

ratings.output_quality_reason: The output provided useful recommendations for reporting requirements, KPIs, and data preparation and helped identify how the existing construction workbook could support Power BI reporting. Most recommendations were relevant and actionable, although some required additional review and refinement based on my knowledge of the workbook.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude successfully analyzed the workbook structure and helped identify reporting requirements, potential KPIs, data limitations, and recommended next steps.  I still needed to apply my own judgement to determine which recommendations were appropriate for the existing workbook.
